headline: Getting the Details Right: What to Look for in Trim and Molding Installation
articleBody: When you're looking to install new trim and molding, paying attention to the details upfront can make all the difference in the final look and feel of your home. It's not just about nailing up some wood; it's about craftsmanship. One critical detail is how inside corners are handled. Will they be coped for a tighter, more professional fit that accommodates natural wood movement, or simply mitered, which can lead to gaps over time? Ask your installer for their approach. You'll also want to understand how seams and joints will be finished. A skilled professional will ensure these are practically invisible, creating a continuous, elegant line around your room. Don't shy away from asking about their specific techniques for baseboards, casing, and especially crown molding—each requires different considerations for a perfect fit. And always, always ask to see examples of their past trim work. Photos can tell you a lot about their precision and attention to detail. Prioritizing precision, proven detail work, and stain-grade competence in your choice of installer will lead to a result you'll love.
